rationale: Custom Actions Pages workflows require enabling repository workflow publishing first; chosen workflow branches are separate from branch-source publishing. Article covers FPT/GHEC/GHES but plan/runner/native availability still require actual target evidence. configure-pages@v5 gathers metadata and supports static generators; snippets described under jobs actually require a job steps context. Action tag/snippet alone is not immutable reviewed code or a complete runnable workflow. Pages upload artifact is gzip containing one tar; tar under 10 GB and should contain no symbolic/hard links. Archive transport bound is separate from published-site 1 GB bound in limits guide; larger archive allowance does not override site size. Upload action version differs cloud v4 versus GHES v2; deploy action cloud v4 versus GHES v3. Historical tagged examples require client/platform compatibility checks, not assumed current immutable implementations. Deployment minimum pages write and id-token write permissions are required; first example additionally contents read. Declared permissions are necessary configuration, not effective grant or successful native deployment evidence. needs text says build step ID, but YAML uses job identifiers jekyll-build/build. Preserve terminology error; job dependency prevents premature independent artifact search, not proof artifact identity or meaningful tests. Deployment environment is required for branch/deployment protections, default github-pages; environment existence/reference is not proof reviewed protection settings, authorized bypass or enforced denial behavior. Environment URL derives deployment step page_url output. Displayed output URL is not effective site availability/privacy, trusted DNS or successful behavior receipt. Two-job example links build/deploy and uses checkout v6, configure-pages v5, jekyll-build-pages v1 with site destination and versioned artifact actions. It omits explicit deploy permissions compared with preceding required list; surrounding inherited permissions cannot be presumed absent or sufficient without context. Single-job no-build example checks out/configures/uploads whole directory path dot then deploys; no-build does not mean no artifact or permission requirements. Whole-directory upload requires secret/private/source content exclusion review before publication, not default safe packaging. All runner examples use ubuntu-latest unconditionally despite declared GHES scope and self-hosted requirement elsewhere. Preserve mismatch; cloud/GHES action version branches do not make runner configuration universally valid. Build/test sequencing and environment rules remain intended configuration; later abbreviated snippets omit triggers/global context. No workflow created/run, token/environment changed, dependencies executed, site published or rights cleared; linked Marketplace/workflow docs remain separately scoped. Full source and previously reviewed checkout/product context read; candidate accounting is not independent source/published completeness.
